class Host:
    """
    The only supported way for a plugin to reach the editor.

    The core is free to change behind this class; a plugin should never need
    `mu.logic`, `mu.interface` or `mu.modes` internals. One Host is created per
    editor window and handed to every plugin's `register`/`unregister`.
    """

    #: The plugin API version this core provides.
    api_version = PLUGIN_API_VERSION

    def __init__(self, editor, view):
        self._editor = editor
        self._view = view
        self._modes = {}  # short_name -> mode instance
        self._owners = {}  # short_name -> owning plugin (None for the core)
        self._image_dirs = []  # (owning plugin or None, folder) pairs
        self._runner = None  # the program started by run_program
        self._panes = []  # (mode short_name, dock) for each add_pane
        self._plugins = []
        self._loading = None  # the plugin whose register() is running
        #: What happened to each discovered plugin (mu.plugin.loader.PluginRecord),
        #: filled in at startup by app.setup_modes.
        self.plugin_records = []
        #: The plugin environment's status at startup (plugin_env.MISSING,
        #: READY or PYTHON_CHANGED), set by app.setup_modes.
        self.plugin_env_status = None
        # Reports errors in plugin code so they don't crash Nu (see errors.py).
        self._error_handler = PluginErrorHandler(self)

    # --- plugin lifecycle (used by the core) ---

    @property
    def modes(self):
        """The registered modes, as a {short_name: mode} dict (a copy)."""
        return dict(self._modes)

    @property
    def plugins(self):
        """The successfully loaded plugins, in load order (a copy)."""
        return list(self._plugins)

    def load_plugin(self, plugin):
        """
        Check `plugin` is compatible and call its `register`. Return True if
        it loaded.

        This never raises: an incompatible plugin, or one whose `register`
        fails, is logged and skipped, and any modes it registered before
        failing are removed again.
        """
        name = getattr(plugin, "name", repr(plugin))
        reason = check_compatible(getattr(plugin, "api_version", None))
        if reason:
            logger.warning("Skipping plugin %s: %s", name, reason)
            return False
        self._loading = plugin
        try:
            plugin.register(self)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Plugin %s failed to register; skipping it", name)
            self._remove_modes_of(plugin)
            self._remove_images_of(plugin)
            return False
        finally:
            self._loading = None
        self._plugins.append(plugin)
        logger.info("Loaded plugin %s", name)
        return True

    def unload_plugin(self, plugin):
        """
        Call `plugin.unregister` and remove the modes it registered. Errors in
        `unregister` are logged, not raised.
        """
        name = getattr(plugin, "name", repr(plugin))
        try:
            plugin.unregister(self)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Plugin %s failed to unregister", name)
        for short_name, owner in list(self._owners.items()):
            if owner is plugin:
                self._remove_panes_of(short_name)
        self._remove_modes_of(plugin)
        self._remove_images_of(plugin)
        if plugin in self._plugins:
            self._plugins.remove(plugin)
        logger.info("Unloaded plugin %s", name)

    def describe_plugins(self):
        """
        Every discovered plugin as the Plugins tab shows it (see
        `loader.describe`), with the names of the modes each one added.
        """
        rows = loader.describe(
            self.plugin_records,
            modes_of=lambda plugin: [mode.name for mode in self._modes_of(plugin)],
        )
        environment = plugin_env.plugin_env
        for row in rows:
            added = row["kind"] == "added" and bool(row["distribution"])
            # Plugins the learner added can be removed, and updated from PyPI
            # unless they came from a file.
            row["removable"] = added
            row["updatable"] = added and not environment.installed_from_file(
                row["distribution"]
            )
        return rows

    @property
    def plugins_folder(self):
        """The folder Nu loads drop-in plugins from."""
        return loader.DROPIN_DIR

    def set_plugin_enabled(self, plugin_id, enabled):
        """
        Switch the plugin `plugin_id` on or off from the next start. Switching
        a plugin that's loaded back on also forgets its errors this session,
        so Nu offers to switch it off again if it keeps failing.
        """
        loader.set_plugin_enabled(plugin_id, enabled)
        if enabled:
            for record in self.plugin_records:
                if record.id == plugin_id and record.plugin is not None:
                    self._error_handler.forget(record.plugin)

    # --- adding and removing plugins (for the core's Plugins tab) ---

    def plugin_environment_state(self):
        """
        What the Plugins tab says about the plugin environment: its "status"
        at startup (see plugin_env), the "python" it was made with and Nu's
        ("nu_python"), the names of the plugins the learner "added", and its
        "path".
        """
        environment = plugin_env.plugin_env
        return {
            "status": self.plugin_env_status,
            "python": environment.python(),
            "nu_python": plugin_env.python_version(),
            "added": [entry["name"] for entry in environment.added()],
            "path": environment.path,
        }

    def check_plugin_name(self, text):
        """
        The requirement (a packaging Requirement) for the plugin package the
        learner typed, if Nu can add it. Raises plugin_env.PluginInputError
        with a sentence for them if it's not a plain package name, or if Nu
        already has it.
        """
        requirement = plugin_env.parse_requirement(text)
        self._check_not_already_there(requirement.name)
        return requirement

    def check_plugin_file(self, path):
        """
        The (name, version) of the plugin wheel file at `path`, if Nu can add
        it. Raises plugin_env.PluginInputError as `check_plugin_name` does. A
        file of a plugin the learner already added replaces it.
        """
        name, version = plugin_env.wheel_name(path)
        self._check_not_already_there(name, added_ok=True)
        return name, version

    def look_up_plugin(self, name):
        """
        What PyPI says about the package `name` (see
        plugin_env.fetch_pypi_info), or None if there's no such package.
        Blocks, and raises OSError without the internet: call it off the GUI
        thread.
        """
        return plugin_env.fetch_pypi_info(name)

    def _check_not_already_there(self, name, added_ok=False):
        environment = plugin_env.plugin_env
        key = canonicalize_name(name)
        if key in plugin_env.NU_DISTRIBUTIONS or key in environment.nu_distributions():
            raise plugin_env.PluginInputError(
                _("Nu already has {name}: it's part of Nu.").format(name=name)
            )
        if not added_ok and environment.exists() and environment.distribution(name):
            raise plugin_env.PluginInputError(
                _(
                    "You've already added {name}. To get its latest version, "
                    "pick it in the list and click Update."
                ).format(name=name)
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _learner_uv():
        """The Uv for the learner's Python environment, if it's there."""
        if not os.path.isfile(venv.interpreter):
            return None
        return venv._uv()

    def add_plugin(self, requirement=None, wheel=None):
        """
        A plugin_env.PluginJob that adds the plugin `requirement` (from
        `check_plugin_name`) or the wheel file `wheel` to the plugin
        environment, then its learner-env packages to the learner's. The
        Plugins tab runs it; it takes effect at the next start.
        """
        return plugin_env.add_job(
            plugin_env.plugin_env,
            requirement=requirement,
            wheel=wheel,
            learner_uv=self._learner_uv,
        )

    def update_plugin(self, distribution):
        """A job updating the added plugin package `distribution`."""
        return plugin_env.update_job(
            plugin_env.plugin_env, distribution, learner_uv=self._learner_uv
        )

    def remove_plugin(self, distribution):
        """A job removing the added plugin package `distribution`."""
        return plugin_env.remove_job(plugin_env.plugin_env, distribution)

    def reinstall_plugins(self):
        """
        A job making the plugin environment again with Nu's Python, with
        every plugin the learner added (for after Nu moved to a new Python).
        """
        return plugin_env.reinstall_job(
            plugin_env.plugin_env, learner_uv=self._learner_uv
        )

    def _modes_of(self, plugin):
        """The mode instances `plugin` registered."""
        return [
            self._modes[name] for name, owner in self._owners.items() if owner is plugin
        ]

    def _remove_modes_of(self, plugin):
        for short_name, owner in list(self._owners.items()):
            if owner is plugin:
                mode = self._modes.pop(short_name)
                del self._owners[short_name]
                try:
                    mode.stop()
                except Exception:
                    logger.exception("Mode %s failed to stop", short_name)

    def _remove_images_of(self, plugin):
        for owner, directory in list(self._image_dirs):
            if owner is plugin:
                resources.unregister_image_dir(directory)
                self._image_dirs.remove((owner, directory))

    # --- registration (call from Plugin.register) ---

    def register_mode(self, mode_class):
        """
        Create an instance of `mode_class` (a `mu.plugin.Mode` subclass) and
        make it available in the editor. Its `short_name` must be unique.
        Returns the new mode instance, whose `host` attribute is this Host.
        """
        if not (isinstance(mode_class, type) and issubclass(mode_class, BaseMode)):
            raise TypeError("{!r} is not a Mode subclass".format(mode_class))
        short_name = mode_class.short_name
        if short_name in self._modes:
            raise ValueError(
                "A mode called {!r} is already registered".format(short_name)
            )
        mode = mode_class(self._editor, self._view)
        mode.host = self
        if self._loading is not None:
            # A plugin's mode: errors in the methods the core calls are
            # reported instead of crashing Nu.
            self._error_handler.guard_mode(mode, self._loading)
        # Whatever deactivate does, the mode's panes go when it's left.
        deactivate = mode.deactivate

        def deactivate_and_remove_panes(*args, **kwargs):
            try:
                return deactivate(*args, **kwargs)
            finally:
                self._remove_panes_of(short_name)

        mode.deactivate = deactivate_and_remove_panes
        self._modes[short_name] = mode
        self._owners[short_name] = self._loading
        return mode

    def register_images(self, directory):
        """
        Make the images in `directory` (a str or os.PathLike) available by
        name, after Nu's own: a mode's `icon`, an action's `name` and
        `update_action(icon=...)` then find `name.svg` / `name.png` there.

        Every image name must be new. If one matches an image Nu or another
        plugin already has, this raises ValueError naming it, so the plugin
        fails to register and is skipped. The images are removed again when
        the plugin unloads.
        """
        resources.register_image_dir(directory)
        self._image_dirs.append((self._loading, directory))

    # --- talking to the learner ---

    def show_message(self, message, information=None, icon=None):
        """
        Show a modal message. `icon` is one of "NoIcon", "Question",
        "Information", "Warning" (the default) or "Critical".
        """
        self._view.show_message(message, information, icon)

    def confirm(self, message, information=None, icon=None):
        """
        Ask the learner to confirm with OK/Cancel; return True for OK. `icon`
        is as for `show_message`.
        """
        result = self._view.show_confirmation(message, information, icon)
        return result == QMessageBox.StandardButton.Ok

    def show_status(self, message, duration=5):
        """Show `message` in the status bar for `duration` seconds."""
        self._editor.show_status_message(message, duration)

    # --- the editor's state ---

    def current_text(self):
        """The text in the current tab, or None if no tab is open."""
        tab = self._view.current_tab
        return tab.text() if tab else None

    def current_path(self):
        """The file path of the current tab, or None if unsaved or no tab."""
        tab = self._view.current_tab
        return tab.path if tab else None

    def workspace_dir(self):
        """The learner's workspace directory (where files are saved)."""
        return BaseMode.workspace_dir()

    @property
    def current_device(self):
        """
        The board picked in the device selector (a `mu.plugin.Device`), or
        None if there's none. A property.
        """
        return self._editor.current_device

    def open_directory(self, path):
        """Open `path` in the operating system's file manager."""
        self._view.open_directory_from_os(path)

    def save_current(self):
        """
        Save the current tab, asking the learner for a file name if it has
        none yet. Return its path, or None if there's no tab or the learner
        cancelled naming it.
        """
        tab = self._view.current_tab
        if tab is None:
            return None
        if tab.path is None:
            self._editor.save()  # asks for a name
        if tab.path and tab.isModified():
            self._editor.save_tab_to_file(tab)
        return tab.path

    def update_action(self, name, display_name=None, description=None, icon=None):
        """
        Change the toolbar button for the current mode's action `name`: its
        label, its tooltip and/or its icon (an image name, looked up like a
        mode's icons). Anything not given is left as it is. Raises ValueError
        if there's no such button (e.g. another mode is current).
        """
        slot = self._view.button_bar.slots.get(name)
        if slot is None:
            raise ValueError("There's no toolbar button called {!r}".format(name))
        if icon is not None:
            slot.setIcon(resources.load_icon(icon))
        if display_name is not None:
            slot.setText(display_name)
        if description is not None:
            slot.setToolTip(description)

    # --- running the learner's program ---

    def run_program(self, path, python_args=None, interactive=False):
        """
        Run the Python program at `path` the way the Run button does: with the
        learner's Python environment and environment variables, from the
        program's folder, its output in the output pane. `python_args` go to
        Python before the program (e.g. `["-m", "pgzero"]`); `interactive`
        leaves a Python prompt open when it finishes. Return True if it
        started. Save it first (see `save_current`).

        A program with a ``# /// script`` block (PEP 723 inline
        dependencies) runs with ``uv run … --with-requirements <path> python
        <python_args> <path>``, which adds the packages it lists on top of
        the learner's environment; there's no Python prompt afterwards then.
        """
        cwd = os.path.dirname(path)
        envars = self._editor.envars
        record = None
        if wants_uv_run(_read_text(path)):
            run_args = [*(python_args or []), path]
            try:
                record = venv.with_requirements_command(path, run_args, cwd)
            except UvNotFound:
                logger.exception("No uv to run a script with inline metadata.")
                self.show_message(
                    _("Nu can't find uv, so it can't run this program."),
                    _(
                        "This program starts with a “# /// script” block "
                        "listing the packages it needs, and Nu uses uv to "
                        "fetch them. Reinstalling Nu should bring uv back. Or "
                        "remove the block to run the program with your "
                        "environment's packages."
                    ),
                )
                return False
            self._runner = self._view.add_python3_runner(
                interpreter=record.program,
                script_name=path,
                working_directory=cwd,
                interactive=False,
                envars=envars,
                python_args=record.argv[1:-1],
                echo="$ " + record.display(),
            )
        else:
            self._runner = self._view.add_python3_runner(
                interpreter=venv.interpreter,
                script_name=path,
                working_directory=cwd,
                interactive=interactive,
                envars=envars,
                python_args=python_args,
            )
        if self._runner is None:
            return False
        if record is not None:
            self._runner.track_uv_command(record)
        self._runner.process.waitForStarted()
        return True

    def add_pane(self, widget, title, area="bottom"):
        """
        Dock `widget` (your own Qt widget, e.g. a file list) in Nu's window
        with `title`, at `area`: "bottom" (the default), "left" or "right",
        as the REPL and plotter are docked; the learner can move it. If the
        widget has a `set_theme(theme)` method it's called with "day",
        "night" or "contrast" now and whenever the theme changes. Returns a
        handle for `remove_pane`.

        The pane belongs to the current mode: Nu removes it when the learner
        leaves the mode (after its `deactivate`) or the plugin unloads.
        """
        dock = self._view.add_plugin_pane(widget, title, area)
        self._panes.append((self._editor.mode, dock))
        return dock

    def remove_pane(self, pane):
        """
        Take away a pane `add_pane` docked. Does nothing if it's already
        gone (e.g. its mode was left).
        """
        for entry in list(self._panes):
            if entry[1] is pane:
                self._panes.remove(entry)
                self._view.remove_plugin_pane(pane)

    def _remove_panes_of(self, short_name):
        """Remove the panes added while the mode `short_name` was current."""
        for mode_name, dock in list(self._panes):
            if mode_name == short_name:
                self.remove_pane(dock)

    def open_file(self, path):
        """
        Open the file at `path` in a tab, as if the learner had loaded it
        (or go to its tab if it's already open).
        """
        self._editor.direct_load(path)

    def stop_program(self):
        """Stop the program `run_program` started, and close its pane."""
        if self._runner:
            self._runner.stop_process()
            self._runner = None
        self._view.remove_python_runner()

    def python_apis(self):
        """
        The autocomplete and call tip entries of Nu's Python 3 mode (Python's
        built-ins and standard library, and common Raspberry Pi libraries),
        as a new list a mode's `api()` can add its own to.
        """
        return SHARED_APIS + PYTHON3_APIS + PI_APIS

    def shared_apis(self):
        """
        The autocomplete and call tip entries every Python has, MicroPython
        and CircuitPython included (built-ins, and str, list and dict
        methods), as a new list a MicroPython-family mode's `api()` can add
        its board's own to.
        """
        return list(SHARED_APIS)

    @property
    def plotter_available(self):
        """
        True if Nu can show the plotter (the optional PyQt6-Charts package is
        installed). Offer a Plotter button (`MicroPythonMode.toggle_plotter`)
        only when it is.
        """
        # Read when asked, not at import: the panes module is the one place
        # that knows whether Qt Charts imported.
        from ..interface import panes

        return panes.CHARTS

    # --- housekeeping ---

    def settings(self, namespace):
        """Settings that persist between sessions, private to `namespace`."""
        return PluginSettings(namespace)

    def data_dir(self, name):
        """
        A folder of the plugin's own in Nu's data folder, for files it
        downloads or caches (not the learner's work, which belongs in the
        workspace). `name` is a plain folder name, normally the plugin's id:
        `data_dir("microbit")` is `<Nu's data folder>/microbit`. It's made if
        missing; returns its path.
        """
        if (
            not isinstance(name, str)
            or name in ("", ".", "..")
            or "/" in name
            or "\\" in name
        ):
            raise ValueError("{!r} isn't a plain folder name".format(name))
        path = os.path.join(config.DATA_DIR, name)
        os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
        return path

    def log_command(self, argv, cwd=None, note=None):
        """
        Record a command in the log the learner sees under "What Nu Ran"
        (and in Nu's log file), as uv's commands are: `argv` is the command
        as the learner could type it (`["mpremote", "connect", port, ...]`),
        `cwd` the folder it runs in, `note` a sentence for anything they
        should know (e.g. that Nu did the same thing through the program's
        Python API rather than running it). Returns the
        `mu.command_log.CommandRecord`: call its `add_output(text)` as
        output arrives and `finish(exit_code, output=None)` when it's done
        (0 for success). Safe to call from any thread.
        """
        return command_log.start(argv, cwd=cwd, note=note)

    def logger(self, name):
        """A logger whose output goes to Nu's log file, as "mu.plugins.<name>"."""
        return logging.getLogger("mu.plugins." + name)

Dock widget (your own Qt widget, e.g. a file list) in Nu's window with title, at area: "bottom" (the default), "left" or "right", as the REPL and plotter are docked; the learner can move it. If the widget has a set_theme(theme) method it's called with "day", "night" or "contrast" now and whenever the theme changes. Returns a handle for remove_pane.

def add_pane(self, widget, title, area="bottom"):
    """
    Dock `widget` (your own Qt widget, e.g. a file list) in Nu's window
    with `title`, at `area`: "bottom" (the default), "left" or "right",
    as the REPL and plotter are docked; the learner can move it. If the
    widget has a `set_theme(theme)` method it's called with "day",
    "night" or "contrast" now and whenever the theme changes. Returns a
    handle for `remove_pane`.

    The pane belongs to the current mode: Nu removes it when the learner
    leaves the mode (after its `deactivate`) or the plugin unloads.
    """
    dock = self._view.add_plugin_pane(widget, title, area)
    self._panes.append((self._editor.mode, dock))
    return dock

def data_dir(self, name):
    """
    A folder of the plugin's own in Nu's data folder, for files it
    downloads or caches (not the learner's work, which belongs in the
    workspace). `name` is a plain folder name, normally the plugin's id:
    `data_dir("microbit")` is `<Nu's data folder>/microbit`. It's made if
    missing; returns its path.
    """
    if (
        not isinstance(name, str)
        or name in ("", ".", "..")
        or "/" in name
        or "\\" in name
    ):
        raise ValueError("{!r} isn't a plain folder name".format(name))
    path = os.path.join(config.DATA_DIR, name)
    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    return path

def describe_plugins(self):
    """
    Every discovered plugin as the Plugins tab shows it (see
    `loader.describe`), with the names of the modes each one added.
    """
    rows = loader.describe(
        self.plugin_records,
        modes_of=lambda plugin: [mode.name for mode in self._modes_of(plugin)],
    )
    environment = plugin_env.plugin_env
    for row in rows:
        added = row["kind"] == "added" and bool(row["distribution"])
        # Plugins the learner added can be removed, and updated from PyPI
        # unless they came from a file.
        row["removable"] = added
        row["updatable"] = added and not environment.installed_from_file(
            row["distribution"]
        )
    return rows

docs.title: load_plugin(plugin)
docs.text:
Check plugin is compatible and call its register. Return True if it loaded.

This never raises: an incompatible plugin, or one whose register fails, is logged and skipped, and any modes it registered before failing are removed again.

Source code in mu/plugin/host.py 
def load_plugin(self, plugin):
    """
    Check `plugin` is compatible and call its `register`. Return True if
    it loaded.

    This never raises: an incompatible plugin, or one whose `register`
    fails, is logged and skipped, and any modes it registered before
    failing are removed again.
    """
    name = getattr(plugin, "name", repr(plugin))
    reason = check_compatible(getattr(plugin, "api_version", None))
    if reason:
        logger.warning("Skipping plugin %s: %s", name, reason)
        return False
    self._loading = plugin
    try:
        plugin.register(self)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Plugin %s failed to register; skipping it", name)
        self._remove_modes_of(plugin)
        self._remove_images_of(plugin)
        return False
    finally:
        self._loading = None
    self._plugins.append(plugin)
    logger.info("Loaded plugin %s", name)
    return True

docs.title: register_mode(mode_class)
docs.text:
Create an instance of mode_class (a mu.plugin.Mode subclass) and make it available in the editor. Its short_name must be unique. Returns the new mode instance, whose host attribute is this Host.

Source code in mu/plugin/host.py 
def register_mode(self, mode_class):
    """
    Create an instance of `mode_class` (a `mu.plugin.Mode` subclass) and
    make it available in the editor. Its `short_name` must be unique.
    Returns the new mode instance, whose `host` attribute is this Host.
    """
    if not (isinstance(mode_class, type) and issubclass(mode_class, BaseMode)):
        raise TypeError("{!r} is not a Mode subclass".format(mode_class))
    short_name = mode_class.short_name
    if short_name in self._modes:
        raise ValueError(
            "A mode called {!r} is already registered".format(short_name)
        )
    mode = mode_class(self._editor, self._view)
    mode.host = self
    if self._loading is not None:
        # A plugin's mode: errors in the methods the core calls are
        # reported instead of crashing Nu.
        self._error_handler.guard_mode(mode, self._loading)
    # Whatever deactivate does, the mode's panes go when it's left.
    deactivate = mode.deactivate

    def deactivate_and_remove_panes(*args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return deactivate(*args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            self._remove_panes_of(short_name)

    mode.deactivate = deactivate_and_remove_panes
    self._modes[short_name] = mode
    self._owners[short_name] = self._loading
    return mode

docs.title: run_program(path, python_args=None, interactive=False)
docs.text:
Run the Python program at path the way the Run button does: with the learner's Python environment and environment variables, from the program's folder, its output in the output pane. python_args go to Python before the program (e.g. ["-m", "pgzero"]); interactive leaves a Python prompt open when it finishes. Return True if it started. Save it first (see save_current).

A program with a # /// script block (PEP 723 inline dependencies) runs with uv run … --with-requirements <path> python <python_args> <path>, which adds the packages it lists on top of the learner's environment; there's no Python prompt afterwards then.

Source code in mu/plugin/host.py 
def run_program(self, path, python_args=None, interactive=False):
    """
    Run the Python program at `path` the way the Run button does: with the
    learner's Python environment and environment variables, from the
    program's folder, its output in the output pane. `python_args` go to
    Python before the program (e.g. `["-m", "pgzero"]`); `interactive`
    leaves a Python prompt open when it finishes. Return True if it
    started. Save it first (see `save_current`).

    A program with a ``# /// script`` block (PEP 723 inline
    dependencies) runs with ``uv run … --with-requirements <path> python
    <python_args> <path>``, which adds the packages it lists on top of
    the learner's environment; there's no Python prompt afterwards then.
    """
    cwd = os.path.dirname(path)
    envars = self._editor.envars
    record = None
    if wants_uv_run(_read_text(path)):
        run_args = [*(python_args or []), path]
        try:
            record = venv.with_requirements_command(path, run_args, cwd)
        except UvNotFound:
            logger.exception("No uv to run a script with inline metadata.")
            self.show_message(
                _("Nu can't find uv, so it can't run this program."),
                _(
                    "This program starts with a “# /// script” block "
                    "listing the packages it needs, and Nu uses uv to "
                    "fetch them. Reinstalling Nu should bring uv back. Or "
                    "remove the block to run the program with your "
                    "environment's packages."
                ),
            )
            return False
        self._runner = self._view.add_python3_runner(
            interpreter=record.program,
            script_name=path,
            working_directory=cwd,
            interactive=False,
            envars=envars,
            python_args=record.argv[1:-1],
            echo="$ " + record.display(),
        )
    else:
        self._runner = self._view.add_python3_runner(
            interpreter=venv.interpreter,
            script_name=path,
            working_directory=cwd,
            interactive=interactive,
            envars=envars,
            python_args=python_args,
        )
    if self._runner is None:
        return False
    if record is not None:
        self._runner.track_uv_command(record)
    self._runner.process.waitForStarted()
    return True

def save_current(self):
    """
    Save the current tab, asking the learner for a file name if it has
    none yet. Return its path, or None if there's no tab or the learner
    cancelled naming it.
    """
    tab = self._view.current_tab

    if tab.path and tab.isModified():
        self._editor.save_tab_to_file(tab)
    return tab.path

def set_plugin_enabled(self, plugin_id, enabled):

    Switch the plugin `plugin_id` on or off from the next start. Switching
    a plugin that's loaded back on also forgets its errors this session,
    so Nu offers to switch it off again if it keeps failing.

def unload_plugin(self, plugin):
    """
    Call `plugin.unregister` and remove the modes it registered. Errors in
    `unregister` are logged, not raised.
    """
    name = getattr(plugin, "name", repr(plugin))
    try:
        plugin.unregister(self)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Plugin %s failed to unregister", name)
    for short_name, owner in list(self._owners.items()):
        if owner is plugin:
            self._remove_panes_of(short_name)
    self._remove_modes_of(plugin)
    self._remove_images_of(plugin)
    if plugin in self._plugins:
        self._plugins.remove(plugin)
    logger.info("Unloaded plugin %s", name)

class PluginSettings:
    """
    A plugin's own corner of the user settings, persisted with them.

    Values live under `settings["plugins"][namespace]`, so plugins can't clash
    with each other or with the core's keys. Values must be JSON-serialisable.
    """

    def __init__(self, namespace, store=None):
        self.namespace = namespace
        self._store = settings.settings if store is None else store

    def _values(self):
        return dict(self._store.get("plugins", {}).get(self.namespace, {}))

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        """Return the value stored under `key`, or `default`."""
        return self._values().get(key, default)

    def set(self, key, value):
        """Store `value` under `key`; it is saved with the user's settings."""
        # Rebuild the nested dicts rather than mutating them in place, so the
        # settings object marks "plugins" as changed and saves it.
        values = self._values()
        values[key] = value
        plugins = dict(self._store.get("plugins", {}))
        plugins[self.namespace] = values
        self._store["plugins"] = plugins

    def __contains__(self, key):
        return key in self._values()

def describe(records, store=None, modes_of=None):
    """
    What the Plugins tab shows: a dict per record, in the same order, with
    the record's facts plus `enabled` (whether it will load at the next
    start, from the settings), `switched_off_after_errors`, `can_switch`
    (False for a duplicate id, which is switched with the first plugin of
    that id), `distribution` (its package's name, or "") and `modes` (from
    `modes_of(plugin)`; [] if it isn't loaded).
    """
    disabled = disabled_plugins(store)
    after_errors = switched_off_after_errors(store)
    rows = []
    seen = set()
    for record in records:
        modes = []
        if record.plugin is not None and modes_of is not None:
            modes = list(modes_of(record.plugin))
        rows.append(
            {
                "id": record.id,
                "name": record.name or record.id,
                "description": record.description,
                "kind": record.kind,
                "origin": record.origin,
                "distribution": record.distribution,
                "status": record.status,
                "problem": record.problem,
                "reason": record.reason,
                "detail": record.detail,
                "enabled": record.id not in disabled,
                "switched_off_after_errors": record.id in after_errors,
                "can_switch": record.id not in seen,
                "modes": modes,
            }
        )
        seen.add(record.id)
    return rows

def dropin_sources(dirpath=None):
    """
    Plugins dropped into `dirpath`: each `name.py` file or `name/` package
    (with an `__init__.py`) is one plugin, with id `name`. The folder is
    created if it doesn't exist, so it's there for learners to find.
    Defaults to DROPIN_DIR.
    """
    if dirpath is None:
        dirpath = DROPIN_DIR
    try:
        os.makedirs(dirpath, exist_ok=True)
        entries = sorted(os.listdir(dirpath))
    except OSError:
        logger.exception("Can't read the plugins folder %s", dirpath)
        return []
    sources = []
    for entry in entries:
        path = os.path.join(dirpath, entry)
        if entry.startswith((".", "_")):
            continue
        if os.path.isdir(path):
            if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path, "__init__.py")):
                continue
            name = entry
        elif entry.endswith(".py"):
            name = entry[:-3]
        else:
            continue
        if not name.isidentifier():
            logger.warning("Ignoring %s: not a valid Python module name", path)
            continue

        def load(name=name, path=path):
            module = _import_dropin(name, path)
            return _instantiate(_dropin_plugin_object(module), name)

        sources.append(PluginSource(name, "folder", path, load))
    return sources

def entry_point_sources(group=ENTRY_POINT_GROUP):
    """
    Plugins installed as packages, found through their `mu.plugins` entry
    points: in the environment Nu runs from, and in the plugin environment
    once it's on `sys.path` (see plugin_env.py), whose are kind "added".
    """
    sources = []
    for entry_point in importlib.metadata.entry_points(group=group):
        dist = entry_point.dist
        kind = "package"
        name = description = dist_name = ""
        if dist:
            origin = "{} {}".format(dist.name, dist.version)
            dist_name = _normalise(dist.name)
            if dist_name in BUNDLED_DISTRIBUTIONS:
                kind = "bundled"
                name = _(BUNDLED_NAMES[dist_name])
            else:
                if plugin_env.plugin_env.contains(dist):
                    kind = "added"
                name = _metadata(dist, "Name")
            description = _metadata(dist, "Summary")
        else:
            origin = entry_point.value

        def load(entry_point=entry_point):
            return _instantiate(entry_point.load(), entry_point.value)

        sources.append(
            PluginSource(
                entry_point.name, kind, origin, load, description, name, dist_name
            )
        )
    return sources

Load every discovered, enabled plugin into host and return a PluginRecord for each one found.

This never raises. A plugin that is switched off, shares an id with one already found, fails to import, targets an incompatible API version or fails in register is recorded (and logged) as skipped, and Nu carries on without it.

Source code in mu/plugin/loader.py 
def load_plugins(host, sources=None, store=None):
    """
    Load every discovered, enabled plugin into `host` and return a
    PluginRecord for each one found.

    This never raises. A plugin that is switched off, shares an id with one
    already found, fails to import, targets an incompatible API version or
    fails in `register` is recorded (and logged) as skipped, and Nu carries
    on without it.
    """
    if sources is None:
        sources = discover()
    disabled = disabled_plugins(store)
    records = []
    seen = set()
    for source in sources:
        record = PluginRecord(
            source.id,
            source.kind,
            source.origin,
            SKIPPED,
            name=source.name or source.id,
            description=source.description,
            distribution=source.distribution,
        )
        records.append(record)
        if source.id in seen:
            record.problem = DUPLICATE
            record.reason = "another plugin is already called {!r}".format(source.id)
            logger.warning("Skipping plugin %s (%s): %s", *_describe(record))
            continue
        seen.add(source.id)
        if source.id in disabled:
            record.status = DISABLED
            logger.info("Plugin %s (%s) is switched off", source.id, source.origin)
            continue
        try:
            plugin = source.load()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            raise
        except BaseException as ex:  # incl. SystemExit from a plugin's import
            record.problem = IMPORT_FAILED
            record.reason = "it failed to import: {}".format(
                "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(ex)).strip()
            )
            record.detail = _plugin_traceback(ex)
            logger.exception("Skipping plugin %s (%s)", source.id, source.origin)
            continue
        if plugin.name == Plugin.name:
            plugin.name = source.id  # unnamed: use its id in logs and the UI
        record.name = plugin.name
        record.description = getattr(plugin, "description", "") or record.description
        reason = check_compatible(getattr(plugin, "api_version", None))
        if reason:
            record.problem = INCOMPATIBLE
            record.reason = reason
            logger.warning("Skipping plugin %s (%s): %s", *_describe(record))
            continue
        if host.load_plugin(plugin):
            record.status = LOADED
            record.plugin = plugin
        else:
            record.problem = REGISTER_FAILED
            record.reason = "it failed to register (see the log)"
    return records

def set_plugin_enabled(plugin_id, enabled, store=None, after_errors=False):
    """
    Switch a plugin on or off; takes effect the next time Nu starts. The
    settings are saved straight away, so the change survives Nu crashing.

    `after_errors` marks a plugin switched off because it kept failing, so
    the Plugins tab can say so. Any other change clears the mark.
    """
    store = settings.settings if store is None else store
    disabled = disabled_plugins(store)
    if enabled:
        disabled.discard(plugin_id)
    else:
        disabled.add(plugin_id)
    store[DISABLED_SETTING] = sorted(disabled)
    marked = switched_off_after_errors(store)
    if after_errors and not enabled:
        marked.add(plugin_id)
    else:
        marked.discard(plugin_id)
    if marked or SWITCHED_OFF_SETTING in store:
        store[SWITCHED_OFF_SETTING] = sorted(marked)
    _save(store)

Keeping Nu running when a plugin has an error.

Copyright (c) 2026 the Nu contributors (see the AUTHORS file).

This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version.

You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License along with this program. If not, see http://www.gnu.org/licenses/.

A plugin's code runs in two ways, and both are covered:

  • The core calls a plugin mode's methods (activate, actions, api, ...). PluginErrorHandler.guard_mode wraps those methods: an error is reported and a safe fallback is returned, so e.g. a mode whose api() fails just has no autocomplete.
  • Qt calls the plugin's button handlers, timers and signal handlers. An error there reaches sys.excepthook; app.excepthook first asks handle_uncaught, which recognises plugin code in the traceback and reports the error instead of letting Nu exit.

A plugin can also start threads. An error in a threading.Thread reaches threading.excepthook (app.thread_excepthook), and one in a Qt QThread or QRunnable reaches sys.excepthook on that thread; both ask handle_uncaught too. The plugin is worked out there, but the report (which shows a dialog) is handed to the main thread, since only it may touch the GUI.

Either way the learner sees a dialog naming the plugin (rate limited, so a failing timer can't bury them in dialogs), the details go to the log, and a plugin that keeps failing is offered to be switched off.

class PluginErrorHandler:
    """
    Reports errors in plugin code to the learner and the log, so Nu keeps
    running. There is one per Host.
    """

    #: Minimum seconds between error dialogs for the same plugin.
    DIALOG_INTERVAL = 30
    #: After this many errors, offer to switch the plugin off.
    SWITCH_OFF_AFTER = 3

    def __init__(self, host, clock=time.monotonic):
        self._host = host
        self._clock = clock
        self._states = {}
        self._dialog_open = False
        # Created on the main thread, with the Host: reports from other
        # threads go through it.
        self._relay = _MainThreadRelay()

    def _state(self, plugin):
        return self._states.setdefault(id(plugin), _PluginState())

    def error_count(self, plugin):
        """How many unexpected errors `plugin` has had this session."""
        return self._state(plugin).errors

    def forget(self, plugin):
        """Start counting `plugin`'s errors afresh, as if Nu had restarted."""
        self._states.pop(id(plugin), None)

    # --- working out whose code failed ---

    def _plugin_modules(self):
        """Map each loaded plugin's top-level module name to the plugin."""
        modules = {}
        for plugin in self._host.plugins:
            classes = [type(plugin)] + [
                type(mode) for mode in self._host._modes_of(plugin)
            ]
            for cls in classes:
                top = cls.__module__.split(".")[0]
                if top not in ("mu", "builtins", "__main__"):
                    modules[top] = plugin
        return modules

    def owner(self, tb):
        """
        The plugin whose code appears in traceback `tb` (the innermost one,
        if several), or None if it's all core code. A frame counts as the
        plugin's if it's in the plugin's modules, or is a method called on
        one of the plugin's modes (e.g. inherited MicroPythonMode code).
        """
        modules = self._plugin_modules()
        modes = {
            id(mode): plugin
            for plugin in self._host.plugins
            for mode in self._host._modes_of(plugin)
        }
        found = None
        for frame, _ in traceback.walk_tb(tb):
            top = frame.f_globals.get("__name__", "").split(".")[0]
            plugin = modules.get(top)
            if plugin is None:
                plugin = modes.get(id(frame.f_locals.get("self")))
            if plugin is not None:
                found = plugin
        return found

    def handle_uncaught(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
        """
        Called from `app.excepthook` and `app.thread_excepthook`. If plugin
        code raised the exception, report it and return True (Nu carries on);
        otherwise return False.

        On a thread other than the main one, the report is queued for the main
        thread, which shows it (and logs it) as soon as it can.
        """
        if issubclass(exc_type, KeyboardInterrupt):
            return False
        try:
            plugin = self.owner(tb)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Couldn't work out where an error came from")
            return False
        if plugin is None:
            return False
        if exc is None:
            exc = exc_type()
        current = threading.current_thread()
        if current is threading.main_thread():
            self.report(plugin, exc, tb)
        else:
            self._relay.call.emit(
                functools.partial(self.report, plugin, exc, tb, thread=current.name)
            )
        return True

    # --- guarding the calls the core makes into plugin modes ---

    def guard_mode(self, mode, plugin):
        """Wrap `mode`'s core-called methods so errors are reported."""
        for name, fallback in GUARDED_MODE_METHODS.items():
            method = getattr(mode, name, None)
            if callable(method):
                setattr(mode, name, self._guarded(plugin, method, name, fallback))

    def _guarded(self, plugin, method, name, fallback):
        @functools.wraps(method)
        def guarded(*args, **kwargs):
            try:
                return method(*args, **kwargs)
            except (Exception, SystemExit) as ex:
                self.report(plugin, ex, ex.__traceback__, where=name)
                return fallback() if fallback else None

        return guarded

    # --- telling the learner ---

    def report(self, plugin, exc, tb=None, where=None, thread=None):
        """
        Tell the learner (and the log) that `plugin` raised `exc`, in the mode
        method `where` or the thread called `thread` if given. Call it on the
        main thread. This never raises.
        """
        try:
            if isinstance(exc, PluginError):
                self._report_expected(plugin, exc)
            else:
                self._report_unexpected(plugin, exc, tb, where, thread)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Failed to report an error in plugin %s", plugin)

    def _report_expected(self, plugin, exc):
        logger.info("Plugin %s: %s", plugin.name, exc.message)
        if self._dialog_open:
            self._host.show_status(exc.message)
            return
        self._show_dialog(
            self._host.show_message, exc.message, exc.information, "Information"
        )

    def _report_unexpected(self, plugin, exc, tb, where, thread):
        state = self._state(plugin)
        state.errors += 1
        signature = (type(exc).__name__, str(exc), where)
        location = " in {}()".format(where) if where else ""
        if thread:
            location += " in thread {!r}".format(thread)
        if signature in state.seen:
            logger.error(
                "Plugin %s failed again%s: %s: %s (error #%d)",
                plugin.name,
                location,
                type(exc).__name__,
                exc,
                state.errors,
            )
        else:
            state.seen.add(signature)
            logger.error(
                "Plugin %s failed%s",
                plugin.name,
                location,
                exc_info=(type(exc), exc, tb or exc.__traceback__),
            )

        now = self._clock()
        recently = (
            state.last_dialog is not None
            and now - state.last_dialog < self.DIALOG_INTERVAL
        )
        if self._dialog_open or recently:
            self._host.show_status(
                _("The {} plugin had another problem (see the log).").format(
                    plugin.name
                )
            )
            return
        state.last_dialog = now

        plugin_id = self._plugin_id(plugin)
        if (
            state.errors >= self.SWITCH_OFF_AFTER
            and plugin_id
            and not state.offered_switch_off
        ):
            state.offered_switch_off = True
            message = _("The {} plugin keeps having problems.").format(plugin.name)
            information = _(
                "Nu is still running. Switch the plugin off? It won't be "
                "loaded the next time Nu starts. You can switch it back on in "
                "the Plugins tab of Nu's administration window (the cog in "
                "the status bar)."
            )
            if self._show_dialog(self._host.confirm, message, information, "Question"):
                loader.set_plugin_enabled(plugin_id, False, after_errors=True)
                self._host.show_status(
                    _("The {} plugin is switched off from the next start.").format(
                        plugin.name
                    )
                )
            return

        message = _(
            "The {} plugin had a problem and stopped what it was doing."
        ).format(plugin.name)
        information = _(
            "Nu is still running, so you can carry on. If it keeps happening, "
            "tell the plugin's author:\n\n{}: {}\n\nThe full details are in "
            "Nu's log."
        ).format(type(exc).__name__, exc)
        self._show_dialog(self._host.show_message, message, information, "Warning")

    def _show_dialog(self, show, message, information, icon):
        # A modal dialog runs a nested event loop, so a plugin timer can fail
        # again while it's open; those errors go to the status bar instead.
        self._dialog_open = True
        try:
            return show(message, information, icon)
        finally:
            self._dialog_open = False

    def _plugin_id(self, plugin):
        for record in self._host.plugin_records:
            if record.plugin is plugin:
                return record.id
        return None

def handle_uncaught(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
    """
    Called from `app.excepthook` and `app.thread_excepthook`. If plugin
    code raised the exception, report it and return True (Nu carries on);
    otherwise return False.

    On a thread other than the main one, the report is queued for the main
    thread, which shows it (and logs it) as soon as it can.
    """
    if issubclass(exc_type, KeyboardInterrupt):
        return False
    try:
        plugin = self.owner(tb)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Couldn't work out where an error came from")
        return False
    if plugin is None:
        return False
    if exc is None:
        exc = exc_type()
    current = threading.current_thread()
    if current is threading.main_thread():
        self.report(plugin, exc, tb)
    else:
        self._relay.call.emit(
            functools.partial(self.report, plugin, exc, tb, thread=current.name)
        )
    return True

def owner(self, tb):
    """
    The plugin whose code appears in traceback `tb` (the innermost one,
    if several), or None if it's all core code. A frame counts as the
    plugin's if it's in the plugin's modules, or is a method called on
    one of the plugin's modes (e.g. inherited MicroPythonMode code).
    """
    modules = self._plugin_modules()
    modes = {
        id(mode): plugin
        for plugin in self._host.plugins
        for mode in self._host._modes_of(plugin)
    }
    found = None
    for frame, _ in traceback.walk_tb(tb):
        top = frame.f_globals.get("__name__", "").split(".")[0]
        plugin = modules.get(top)
        if plugin is None:
            plugin = modes.get(id(frame.f_locals.get("self")))
        if plugin is not None:
            found = plugin
    return found

def report(self, plugin, exc, tb=None, where=None, thread=None):
    """
    Tell the learner (and the log) that `plugin` raised `exc`, in the mode
    method `where` or the thread called `thread` if given. Call it on the
    main thread. This never raises.
    """
    try:
        if isinstance(exc, PluginError):
            self._report_expected(plugin, exc)
        else:
            self._report_unexpected(plugin, exc, tb, where, thread)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to report an error in plugin %s", plugin)

def handle_uncaught(exc_type, exc, tb):
    """
    For `app.excepthook`: return True if the exception came from a plugin
    and has been reported, so Nu should carry on.
    """
    if _active is None:
        return False
    try:
        return _active.handle_uncaught(exc_type, exc, tb)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Plugin error handling failed")

class ButtonBar(QToolBar):
    """
    Represents the bar of buttons across the top of the editor and defines
    their behaviour.
    """

    def __init__(self, parent):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.setMovable(False)
        self.setIconSize(QSize(64, 64))
        self.setToolButtonStyle(Qt.ToolButtonStyle.ToolButtonTextUnderIcon)
        self.setContextMenuPolicy(Qt.ContextMenuPolicy.PreventContextMenu)
        self.setObjectName("StandardToolBar")
        self.reset()

    def reset(self):
        """
        Resets the button states.
        """
        self.slots = {}
        self.clear()

    def change_mode(self, mode):
        self.reset()
        self.addAction(
            name="modes",
            display_name=_("Mode"),
            tool_text=_("Change Nu's mode of behaviour."),
        )
        self.addSeparator()
        self.addAction(
            name="new",
            display_name=_("New"),
            tool_text=_("Create a new Python script."),
        )
        self.addAction(
            name="load",
            display_name=_("Load"),
            tool_text=_("Load a Python script."),
        )
        self.addAction(
            name="save",
            display_name=_("Save"),
            tool_text=_("Save the current Python script."),
        )
        self.addSeparator()

        for action in mode.actions():
            self.addAction(
                name=action["name"],
                display_name=action["display_name"],
                tool_text=action["description"],
            )

        self.addSeparator()
        self.addAction(
            name="zoom-in",
            display_name=_("Zoom-in"),
            tool_text=_("Zoom in (to make the text bigger)."),
        )
        self.addAction(
            name="zoom-out",
            display_name=_("Zoom-out"),
            tool_text=_("Zoom out (to make the text smaller)."),
        )
        self.addAction(
            name="theme",
            display_name=_("Theme"),
            tool_text=_("Toggle theme between day, night or high contrast."),
        )
        self.addSeparator()
        self.addAction(
            name="check",
            display_name=_("Check"),
            tool_text=_("Check your code for mistakes."),
        )
        if sys.version_info[:2] >= (3, 6):
            self.addAction(
                name="tidy",
                display_name=_("Tidy"),
                tool_text=_("Tidy up the layout of your code."),
            )
        self.addAction(
            name="help",
            display_name=_("Help"),
            tool_text=_("Show help about Nu in a browser."),
        )
        self.addSeparator()
        self.addAction(name="quit", display_name=_("Quit"), tool_text=_("Quit Nu."))

    def set_responsive_mode(self, width, height):
        """
        Compact button bar for when window is very small: smaller icons and
        text and, if the buttons' labels still don't fit in the `width`
        (long translations, such as Ukrainian, below about 1024 px), icons
        only, with the names in their tooltips. Otherwise the last buttons
        (Help and Quit) would be hidden behind Qt's overflow button, which
        a beginner is unlikely to spot.
        """
        font_size = min(DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE, width // 80)
        icon_size = min(64, width // 24)
        self.setIconSize(QSize(icon_size, icon_size))
        stylesheet = "QWidget{font-size: " + str(font_size) + "px;}"
        self.setStyleSheet(stylesheet)
        self.setToolButtonStyle(Qt.ToolButtonStyle.ToolButtonTextUnderIcon)
        if self.sizeHint().width() > width:
            self.setToolButtonStyle(Qt.ToolButtonStyle.ToolButtonIconOnly)

    def addAction(self, name, display_name, tool_text):
        """
        Creates an action associated with an icon and name and adds it to the
        widget's slots.
        """
        action = QAction(load_icon(name), display_name, self, toolTip=tool_text)
        super().addAction(action)
        self.slots[name] = action

    def connect(self, name, handler, shortcut=None):
        """
        Connects a named slot to a handler function and optional hot-key
        shortcuts.
        """
        self.slots[name].pyqtConfigure(triggered=handler)
        if shortcut:
            self.slots[name].setShortcut(QKeySequence(shortcut))

class FileTabs(QTabWidget):
    """
    Extend the base class so we can override the removeTab behaviour.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super(FileTabs, self).__init__()
        # We are implementing closable tabs manually
        self.setTabsClosable(False)
        self.setMovable(True)
        self.currentChanged.connect(self.change_tab)
        # Shrink icons to avoid giant tabs
        self.setIconSize(self.iconSize() * 0.75)

    def removeTab(self, tab_id):
        """
        Ask the user before closing the file.
        """
        window = self.nativeParentWidget()
        modified = self.widget(tab_id).isModified()
        if modified:
            msg = "There is un-saved work, closing the tab will cause you to lose it."
            if window.show_confirmation(msg) == QMessageBox.StandardButton.Cancel:
                return
        super(FileTabs, self).removeTab(tab_id)

    def addTab(self, widget, title):
        """
        Add a new tab to the switcher
        """
        # Proxy up to the real addTab
        tab_id = super(FileTabs, self).addTab(widget, title)
        # A widget to put the indicator and close button in
        container = QWidget()
        box = QHBoxLayout(container)
        # We don't want any margins on the layout, that would expand the tab
        box.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
        # Ensure some space between image and button
        box.setSpacing(6)
        # Counterintuitively QImage doesn't show an image, QLabel does
        state_lbl = QLabel(container)
        box.addWidget(state_lbl)
        state_lbl.setPixmap(load_pixmap("document", size=self.iconSize()))

        # Watch for status change to update the dirty indicator
        # We watch here as it's far easier to keep track of state_lbl
        # It does mean we assume all tabs are EditorPane
        @widget.modificationChanged.connect
        def on_modified():
            # Wrapped in a try/except because sometimes state_lbl is destroyed
            # by Qt before widget is GC'd by Python. Since there's no way to
            # easily check the status of state_lbl, wrapping in a try/except
            # for a RuntimeError is the simplest possible solution.
            try:
                if widget.isModified():
                    state_lbl.setPixmap(
                        load_pixmap("document-dirty", size=self.iconSize())
                    )
                else:
                    # This icon is actually empty
                    state_lbl.setPixmap(load_pixmap("document", size=self.iconSize()))
            except RuntimeError:  # pragma: no cover
                pass

        # Setup our own close button since we are overriding the built in one
        close_btn = QPushButton(container)
        box.addWidget(close_btn)
        close_btn.setToolTip(_("Close file"))
        close_btn.setFlat(True)
        close_btn.setIconSize(self.iconSize())
        close_btn.setIcon(load_icon("close-tab"))
        close_btn.show()

        # Handle 'clicked' events
        @close_btn.clicked.connect
        def close():
            # The tab_id isn't constant and may have changed, lookup the
            # current id of the EditorPane
            tab_id = self.indexOf(widget)
            # Close the tab
            self.removeTab(tab_id)

        container.setLayout(box)
        # Add the box, clearly it isn't a button but QTabBar actually takes
        # any QWidget not just buttons
        self.tabBar().setTabButton(tab_id, QTabBar.ButtonPosition.RightSide, container)

        # Return the index of the new page just like the real addTab
        return tab_id

    def change_tab(self, tab_id):
        """
        Update the application title to reflect the name of the file in the
        currently selected tab.
        """
        current_tab = self.widget(tab_id)
        window = self.nativeParentWidget()
        if current_tab:
            window.update_title(current_tab.title)
        else:
            window.update_title(None)

class StatusBar(QStatusBar):
    """
    Defines the look and behaviour of the status bar along the bottom of the
    UI.
    """

    def __init__(self, parent=None, mode="python"):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.mode = mode
        self.msg_duration = 5

        # The learner's Python environment (shown only in modes that use it,
        # see set_environment); click it to see and manage the environment.
        self.env_label = QLabel()
        self.env_label.setObjectName("EnvironmentLabel")
        self.env_label.setCursor(Qt.CursorShape.PointingHandCursor)
        self.env_label.setHidden(True)
        self.addPermanentWidget(self.env_label)

        # Mode selector.
        self.mode_label = QLabel()
        self.mode_label.setToolTip(_("Nu's current mode. Click to change it."))
        self.mode_label.setCursor(Qt.CursorShape.PointingHandCursor)
        self.addPermanentWidget(self.mode_label)
        self.set_mode(mode)

        # Device selector.
        self.device_selector = DeviceSelector()
        self.device_selector.setHidden(True)
        self.addPermanentWidget(self.device_selector)

        # Logs viewer
        self.logs_label = QLabel()
        self.logs_label.setObjectName("AdministrationLabel")
        self.logs_label.setPixmap(load_pixmap("logs", size=QSize(24, 24)))
        self.logs_label.setToolTip(_("Nu Administration"))
        self.addPermanentWidget(self.logs_label)

    def connect_logs(self, handler, shortcut):
        """
        Connect the mouse press event and keyboard shortcut for the log widget
        to the referenced handler function.
        """
        self.logs_label.shortcut = QShortcut(QKeySequence(shortcut), self.parent())
        self.logs_label.shortcut.activated.connect(handler)
        self.logs_label.mousePressEvent = handler

    def connect_mode(self, handler, shortcut=None):
        """
        Connect the mouse press event (and keyboard shortcut, if given) for
        the mode widget to the referenced handler function.
        """
        if shortcut:
            self.mode_label.shortcut = QShortcut(QKeySequence(shortcut), self.parent())
            self.mode_label.shortcut.activated.connect(handler)
        self.mode_label.mousePressEvent = handler

    def connect_environment(self, handler):
        """
        Connect a click on the environment indicator to the referenced
        handler function.
        """
        self.env_label.mousePressEvent = handler

    def set_environment(self, name, version, path):
        """
        Show the environment indicator: "Environment: <name> · Python X.Y".
        `version` is the full Python version (or None if unknown) and `path`
        the environment's folder, shown in the tooltip.
        """
        text = _("Environment: {name}").format(name=name)
        if version:
            short_version = ".".join(version.split(".")[:2])
            text += " · " + _("Python {version}").format(version=short_version)
        self.env_label.setText(text)
        self.env_label.setToolTip(
            _(
                "Your programs run with this Python environment:\n{path}\n\n"
                "Click to see it, and to add or remove packages."
            ).format(path=path)
        )
        self.env_label.setHidden(False)

    def hide_environment(self):
        """
        Hide the environment indicator (for modes that don't use the
        learner's Python environment, e.g. CircuitPython).
        """
        self.env_label.setHidden(True)

    def set_message(self, message, pause=5000):
        """
        Displays a message in the status bar for a certain period of time.
        """
        self.showMessage(message, pause)

    def set_mode(self, mode):
        """
        Updates the mode label to the new mode.
        """
        self.mode_label.setText(mode)

    def device_connected(self, device):
        """
        Show a tooltip whenever a new device connects
        """
        if device.board_name:
            msg = _("Detected new {} device: {}.").format(
                device.long_mode_name, device.board_name
            )
        else:
            msg = _("Detected new {} device.").format(device.long_mode_name)

        self.set_message(msg, self.msg_duration * 1000)

        text += " · " + _("Python {version}").format(version=short_version)
    self.env_label.setText(text)
    self.env_label.setToolTip(
        _(
            "Your programs run with this Python environment:\n{path}\n\n"
            "Click to see it, and to add or remove packages."
        ).format(path=path)
    )
    self.env_label.setHidden(False)
